title: Reserved Instance Utilization

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:billing` events with `lineItem_LineItemType="DiscountedUsage" OR lineItem_LineItemType="RIFee"` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.1.20 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:billing` traffic without `lineItem_LineItemType="DiscountedUsage" OR lineItem_LineItemType="RIFee"`. Confirm UC-4.1.20 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:billing` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:billing" lineItem_LineItemType="DiscountedUsage" OR lineItem_LineItemType="RIFee"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.20_reserved_instance_utiliz_20"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.1.20 — Reserved Instance Utilization: queries AWS `aws:billing` for search criteria `lineItem_LineItemType="DiscountedUsage" OR lineItem_LineItemType="RIFee"` and returns actor, resource, and region context for performance review and change validation.
value: On AWS, detecting 'Reserved Instance Utilization' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.1.20 drives low-priority performance alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Ingest CUR data. Calculate RI utilization by comparing reserved hours against actual usage. Dashboard showing RI coverage percentage and waste. Review monthly.
visualization: Table (RI, type, utilization %), Gauge (overall utilization), Bar chart by instance type.
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable: this cost or advisory feed is not a CIM data model. Use the search in Step 2 on the billing or support API data you ingest.
knownFalsePositives: True-up, RI purchase, and one-time credit lines that are not a recurring waste pattern next month.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:billing`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Ingest CUR data. Calculate RI utilization by comparing reserved hours against actual usage. Dashboard showing RI coverage percentage and waste. Review monthly.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:billing" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:billing" lineItem_LineItemType="DiscountedUsage" OR lineItem_LineItemType="RIFee"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.20_reserved_instance_utiliz_20"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:billing` in `index=aws` to detect reserved instance utilization. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_20_alert` with severity aligned to `low` criticality. Dashboard: Table (RI, type, utilization %), Gauge (overall utilization), Bar chart by instance type..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of reserved instance utilization so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
